findings.title: font='sans-serif' (or any hyphenated family name) crashes hyp.plot with a cryptic fontconfig ParseException instead of the documented helpful error
findings.repro:
cd /tmp && env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
hyp.plot(np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=(10,3)), font='sans-serif', reduce=None, show=False)
"
findings.expected: Either the font resolves (matplotlib accepts 'sans-serif' everywhere else, e.g. FontProperties(family=['sans-serif'])) or the documented ValueError: "font='sans-serif' is not a recognized installed font family... Pass a valid installed family name, a path to a .ttf/.otf/.ttc file, or a ... FontProperties instance."
findings.actual:
ValueError: 
sans-serif
    ^
ParseException: Expected end of text, found '-'  (at char 4), (line:1, col:5)
  [raised from matplotlib/_fontconfig_pattern.py:88 parse_fontconfig_pattern, via FontProperties(family=font) at hypertools/plot/fonts.py:222] | RUN-2 reverified verbatim: ValueError : \nsans-serif\n    ^\nParseException: Expected end of text, found '-'  (at char 4), (line:1, col:5). Crash occurs at FontProperties(family='sans-serif') construction, BEFORE resolve_font's guarded findfont try/except, so the documented helpful ValueError never fires.

findings.title: `import hypertools.plot.colors` / `.fonts` / `.interactive` / `.multiindex` as-import fails: plot() function shadows the plot subpackage, with a cryptic ImportError
findings.expected: Either the import works, or documentation states that plot submodules must be imported via `from hypertools.plot import <mod>`.
findings.actual: ImportError: cannot import name 'interactive' from 'plot' (unknown location)   [also: print(type(hypertools.plot)) -> <class 'function'>; sys.modules['hypertools.plot'] is the real module] | RUN-2: 'import hypertools.plot.fonts as m' -> ImportError: cannot import name 'fonts' from 'plot' (unknown location); plain 'import hypertools.plot.fonts' succeeds but 'hypertools.plot.fonts' attribute access -> AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'fonts'; 'from hypertools.plot import fonts' works. Root cause verified: hypertools/__init__.py line 4 'from .plot.plot import plot' rebinds the attribute.

findings.title: mat2colors docstring omits the signed-matrix per-row-shift semantics and their consequences (2-column signed rows can only be pure vertex colors; one negative row changes the colors of valid non-negative rows)
findings.repro:
/Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np
from hypertools.plot.colors import mat2colors
print(mat2colors(np.array([[0.25, 0.75]])))
print(mat2colors(np.array([[-1.0, 1.0], [0.25, 0.75]]))[1])
print(mat2colors(np.array([[-1.0, 1.0], [-100.0, 100.0]])))
"
findings.expected: Docstring documents: negative inputs are per-row min-shifted before normalizing; mixing signed and non-negative rows changes the non-negative rows' colors; signed k=2 matrices yield only vertex/uniform colors.
findings.actual: [0.25,0.75] alone -> [0.47  0.714 0.73] (correct blend); with a signed row present -> [0.34 0.8288 0.86] (pure c1); [[-1,1],[-100,100]] -> identical rows [[0.34 0.8288 0.86],[0.34 0.8288 0.86]]. Docstring says only: 'Rows are normalized to sum to 1 and each sample's color is the proportion-weighted blend'.

findings.title: Default 'hls' palette is circular: continuous-hue minimum and maximum values are visually indistinguishable (through hyp.plot's default)
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
from hypertools.plot.colors import mat2colors
c = mat2colors(np.linspace(0, 10, 5))
print(c[0], c[-1], np.abs(c[0]-c[-1]).max())
t = np.linspace(0, 4*np.pi, 300)
traj = np.column_stack([np.cos(t), np.sin(t), t/(4*np.pi)])
fig = hyp.plot(traj, '-', hue=t)  # default palette
fig.savefig('/tmp/hls_wrap.png')
"
findings.expected: A continuous hue should use a perceptually ordered (non-circular) default, or the docs should warn that 'hls' wraps; min and max values should be distinguishable.
findings.actual: mat2colors(np.linspace(0,10,5)) first=[0.86 0.3712 0.34], last=[0.86 0.34 0.34]; 'first vs last max abs diff: 0.031200000000000006'. w2a PNG: spiral start and end both render red.
